【P1｜Mr. Utterson】

当前一句话身份：Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield
档案（最新）：occupation：lawyer；personality：blameless past, troubled by old sins；situation：obsessed with finding and seeing Hyde；residence：bachelor house near a church；identity：trustee of Lanyon's sealed packet

至今经历（按时间）：
- Utterson lies awake all night, haunted by Enfield's tale and the faceless figure.
- Utterson keeps watch by the by-street door at all hours until his patience is rewarded.
- Utterson resolves to hunt for Hyde, thinking 'If he be Mr. Hyde, I shall be Mr. Seek.'
- A small plainly dressed man approaches the door with a key, and Utterson accosts him as Mr. Hyde.
- Utterson accosts Hyde and asks to be admitted to see Jekyll.
- Utterson asks to see Hyde's face and studies it.
- Hyde angrily accuses Utterson of lying about Jekyll's description.
- Utterson walks away deeply disturbed by Hyde's appearance.
- Poole tells Utterson that Dr. Jekyll has gone out.
- Poole confirms Hyde has a key and comes by the dissecting room door.
- Poole says all servants have orders to obey Hyde.
- Poole says Hyde never dines there and mostly uses the laboratory.
- Utterson goes home fearing Jekyll is in deep waters.
- Utterson stays behind after Jekyll's dinner to speak with him.
- Utterson raises the subject of Jekyll's will.
- Utterson says he has learned something of young Hyde.
- Utterson offers to help Jekyll out of the matter in confidence.
- Jekyll asks Utterson to help Hyde for his sake when he is gone.
- Utterson promises to bear with Hyde and get his rights for him.
- A sealed envelope addressed to Utterson is found on the victim.
- Utterson identifies the body as Sir Danvers Carew.
- The officer narrates the maid's account and shows the broken stick.
- Utterson recognizes the stick as one he gave Henry Jekyll.
- Utterson offers to take the officer to Hyde's house.
- The old woman lets Utterson and the inspector search Hyde's rooms.
- They find the other half of the stick and a burnt cheque book.
- Utterson is admitted by Poole and received into Jekyll's cabinet.
- Utterson asks Jekyll whether he has heard the news.
- Jekyll swears he will never set eyes on Hyde again.
- Jekyll gives Utterson a letter signed Edward Hyde to judge.
- Jekyll says he burned the envelope and it bore no postmark.
- Jekyll admits Hyde dictated the terms of his will.
- Poole tells Utterson no letter came except by post.
- Utterson hears newsboys crying the murder of an M.P.
- Utterson shows Guest the murderer's autograph letter.
- Guest compares the letter with Jekyll's note and finds them identical.
- Utterson locks the note in his safe and suspects Jekyll of forgery.
- Utterson dines with Jekyll and Lanyon as inseparable friends.
- Jekyll shuts his door against Utterson, Poole reporting he is confined.
- Utterson visits Lanyon and is shocked by his decayed appearance.
- Lanyon refuses to hear Jekyll's name, calling him dead to him.
- Utterson writes to Jekyll, who replies of an incurable quarrel.
- After the funeral Utterson opens Lanyon's sealed envelope.
- The enclosure is not to be opened till Jekyll's death or disappearance.
- Utterson prefers speaking with Poole at the door rather than entering.

【P3｜the man in the middle】
别称：Edward Hyde、Hyde、Mr. Hyde、one Hyde、poor Hyde、the fugitive
当前一句话身份：Tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
档案（最新）：appearance：impressed beholders with a sense of unexpressed deformity；personality：merciless, inspires enduring hatred；situation：vanished from police knowledge；identity：young man Jekyll takes great interest in；residence：a street in Soho
关系：Dr. Jekyll（favourite of Jekyll）、Poole（servant）、the old woman（landlady）、Inspector Newcomen of Scotland Yard（accuser）
至今经历（按时间）：
- Enfield collars the man and brings him back to the group around the child.
- The man tramples over the girl's body and leaves her screaming.
- The doctor turns sick and white with desire to kill the prisoner.
- They threaten scandal and force the man to pay a hundred pounds.
- The man leads them to the door, unlocks it, and returns with gold and a cheque.
- The man offers to stay until the banks open and cash the cheque himself.
- They spend the night in Enfield's chambers and go to the bank next day.
- The will leaves all Jekyll's possessions to Edward Hyde, and Hyde inherits if Jekyll vanishes.
- Utterson asks Lanyon about Hyde, and Lanyon has never heard of him.
- A small plainly dressed man approaches the door with a key, and Utterson accosts him as Mr. Hyde.
- Utterson accosts Hyde and asks to be admitted to see Jekyll.
- Hyde tells Utterson that Dr. Jekyll is from home.
- Utterson asks to see Hyde's face and studies it.
- Hyde gives Utterson his address in Soho.
- Hyde angrily accuses Utterson of lying about Jekyll's description.
- Hyde snarls, unlocks the door, and disappears into the house.
- Jekyll says he takes a great interest in poor Hyde.
- The maid sees Hyde beat an aged beautiful gentleman with white hair to death with a cane.
- The inspector finds several thousand pounds to Hyde's credit at the bank.
- The inspector plans to wait for Hyde at the bank and issue handbills.
- Mr. Hyde had few familiars and was hard to trace.
- Hyde's family could not be traced anywhere.
- Hyde had never been photographed.
- Observers agreed only on a sense of unexpressed deformity in Hyde.
- Hyde vanishes after Sir Danvers's murder; rewards are offered.

[note_g1]
Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield。G. J. Utterson is a lawyer, a kinsman and friend of Richard Enfield, and an old friend of both Dr. Jekyll and Dr. Lanyon. He is a man of blameless past who is troubled by old sins. After Enfield told him of a faceless figure at a by-street door, he lay awake haunted, kept watch by that door, and resolved to hunt for Hyde. He accosted Hyde, studied his face, and was deeply disturbed. He raised Jekyll's will, promised to bear with Hyde, identified Sir Danvers Carew's body, recognized his own stick as the weapon, searched Hyde's rooms, and heard Guest find Hyde's letter identical with Jekyll's hand. He dined with Jekyll and Lanyon, then found Jekyll shut against him and Lanyon refusing Jekyll's name. After Lanyon's funeral he opened the sealed envelope, whose enclosure must wait for Jekyll's death or disappearance. He now prefers speaking with Poole at the door rather than entering.

[note_g2]
Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir。Henry Jekyll is a doctor, connoisseur and old friend of Utterson and Lanyon, known for charities and religion. He is fifty, large, well-made and smooth-faced, with a slyish cast. Over ten years ago Lanyon found him too fanciful and wrong in mind. His will leaves all his possessions to Edward Hyde, who inherits if Jekyll vanishes. When Utterson raised the will and Hyde, Jekyll paled, refused to hear more, called Lanyon a hide-bound pedant, said he could be rid of Hyde whenever he chose, and asked Utterson to help Hyde for his sake. He swore he would never set eyes on Hyde again, gave Utterson Hyde's letter to judge, admitted Hyde dictated the will, then emerged and resumed old friendships. He later shut his door against Utterson, wrote of an incurable quarrel, vowed extreme seclusion and an unnameable punishment. He now confines himself over the laboratory and is silent.

[note_g3]
Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor。Dr. Lanyon is a doctor with a house in Cavendish Square, an old friend of Utterson and formerly of Dr. Jekyll. He is boisterous, decided and theatrical but genuine. Over ten years ago he judged Jekyll too fanciful and wrong in mind. When Utterson asked about Hyde, Lanyon had never heard of him. He dined with Jekyll and Utterson as inseparable friends, but later Utterson found him visibly decayed; Lanyon declared himself a doomed man who would never recover, refused to hear Jekyll's name and called him dead to him. He took to his bed and died within a fortnight. After his funeral Utterson opened the sealed envelope Lanyon left, whose enclosure is not to be opened till Jekyll's death or disappearance. He is dead.

[note_g4]
Elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house。Poole is the elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house, obedient to his master and to Hyde as his superior. He told Utterson that Jekyll had gone out, confirmed Hyde had a key and came by the dissecting room door, said all servants had orders to obey Hyde, and that Hyde never dined there and mostly used the laboratory. He admitted Utterson to Jekyll's cabinet and told him no letter came except by post. He reported that Jekyll had shut his door against Utterson and was confined. Utterson now prefers speaking with Poole at the door rather than entering, and Poole reports that Jekyll confines himself over the laboratory and is silent.

[note_g5]
Utterson's head clerk and handwriting expert。Mr. Guest is Utterson's head clerk and a critic of handwriting. Utterson showed him the murderer's autograph letter, and Guest compared it with Jekyll's note and found the two identical. That is all that is known of him to this point; he remains in Utterson's employ.

[note_g6]
Tramples a girl, pays with a cheque。Edward Hyde is a young man in whom Dr. Jekyll takes great interest, the favourite of Jekyll, and the heir named in Jekyll's will. He is merciless, inspires enduring hatred, and impresses beholders with a sense of unexpressed deformity. He trampled over a girl's body and left her screaming, was forced by threats of scandal to pay a hundred pounds, and led Enfield's group to a door where he returned with gold and a cheque. He later met Utterson at that door, gave his address in Soho, angrily accused Utterson of lying about Jekyll's description, and disappeared into the house. The maid saw him beat Sir Danvers Carew to death with a cane. He had few familiars, no traceable family, no photograph, and several thousand pounds to his credit.
